newsitem.title: UK: Moody's rates Greece's drachma bonds A2.
newsitem.headline: Moody's rates Greece's drachma bonds A2.

text.p: Moody's Investor Service said on Tuesday it had assigned a rating of A2 to drachma-denominated Eurobond of the Hellenic Republic.
"The rating will also apply to outstanding drachma treasury bonds issued in the domestic market," Moody's said in a statement.

"The rating reflects the improvement in the fiscal balances in the past few years, as well as the stronger political resolve to continue with policies consistent with EU convergence," Moody's said. "On the other hand, the debt burden remains among the heaviest in the EU."
The rating agency noted that budgetary adjustments had been made so far mostly on the revenue side.

"The reduction in the 1997 budget deficit is achieved through a combination of revenue enhancing measures -- including the abolition of some tax benefits and allowances and some new taxes-- as well as some expenditure controlling measures," Moody's said. "The latter are aimed at rationalising the wider public sector by improving its efficiency, and thus cutting expenditures in the medium-term."
Moody's said the full impact of these changes, some of which were administrative, was expected to be spread over several years.

"The speed of consolidation of the public sector, through privatisation and restructuring of public enterprises, will be a crucial determinant of Greece's economic performance in the years ahead," Moody's said.
